title: Maharashtra Gen Z Adivasis ask for more
content: In Manjari village, on the outskirts of Pune, tribal students have been protesting for over two weeks with a hunger strike against the Maharashtra government, which they say has not heard them for years. They hope this time their need for better quality education and hostel infrastructure will be seen, and the Supreme Court-mandated employment assured nine years ago will be given. Vinaya Deshpande Pandit speaks with the students, many of whom are first-generation college-goers

content: He distributed more than ₹3.42 crore in incentives to 107 startups and ₹1.79 crore to nine incubators under the Startup Policy

content: In this week’s In Focus-Parley, Experts Apoorvanand and Ganesh Devy discuss whether English should be considered a foreign language in India’s diverse linguistic landscape.

title: Water levels subside in Bihar rivers, reducing flood risks a day after Nepal tragedy
content: Three-metre waves were seen at the Valmikinagar barrage, and the water flow peaked at 1.5 lakh cusecs on August 27 afternoon, but then started decreasing; CM conducts aerial survey to assess flood situation, relief preparations

title: Four Naga civilians killed in Manipur ambush
content: Manipur Chief Minister Yumnan Khemchand Singh and Home Minister Govindas Konthoujam condemned the “senseless violence” and said it “strikes at our collective efforts to restore peace and normalcy”

title: Nepal flood toll hits 392; 288 Indians among 1,468 missing
content: Latest available National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority tally put 910 people missing or “out of contact” in Nepal, which includes MEA’s assessment of 288 Indian citizens remaining “uncontactable” as of late Thursday evening. Nepal has not released a nationality-wise breakup of those dead, leaving the number of Indian fatalities, if any, unconfirmed. Across the border in Tibet, Chinese authorities reported 558 people missing as of Thursday morning.

title: BPCL CMD says mulling E10 petrol option, then walks back
content: “We are looking into various related aspects but nothing has been finalised yet,” said the chief of the oil marketing company that is the leading coordinator for the ethanol blending programme. However, a few hours later, amid growing scrutiny, he claimed that he had been misquoted. “His response is being misquoted to suggest as if E10 is being considered as an option, which is not correct, it said.

title: India expresses readiness for treaty talks with Canada, eyes Rs 4.65 lakh crore trade
content: The two ministers discussed ways to strengthen trade and investment ties and agreed on several areas of economic cooperation. "India expressed its readiness to initiate negotiations on a Bilateral Investment Treaty at the earliest," the joint statement issued after the meeting said. A Bilateral Investment Treaty is an agreement between two countries designed to provide greater protection and certainty to investors from both sides.

title: ‘Test cricket won’: Shubman Gill after Sri Lanka force draw in Colombo
content: Following a thrilling second Test match, India captain Shubman Gill hailed the outcome as a victory after Sri Lanka's determined resistance led to a draw. The Sri Lankan team batted fiercely for 154 overs, earning a hard-fought tie. Gill commended their fighting spirit and particularly noted the potential of spinner Manav Suthar for upcoming Indian squads. This match secured India's series win at 1-0.

title: Parliament may be reconvened, hints Rijiju, brings delimitation bill in focus
content: Though Rijiju made no categorical comment about an immediate session to take up the constitutional amendment bill to implement the law from 2029 with a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats, he said Parliament has been reconvened in the past after a session was not prorogued. The monsoon session, which ended on Aug 13, has not been prorogued yet.

title: A Hawaii retreat, staff revolt, and weak AI: How Meta's 60% layoffs plan came apart
content: Meta explored cutting some teams by up to 60% and handing their work to AI agents under a plan code-named Project OT. Hatched at Mark Zuckerberg's Hawaii retreat, it involved two layoff waves, pods of three replacing traditional teams, and keystroke tracking to train AI models. Staff revolted, internal sentiment fell from 74% to 55%, and Meta's own data showed the AI wasn't delivering promised productivity gains.

title: PM Modi to meet Russia's Putin on SCO meeting sidelines
content: PM Modi’s bilateral with Putin, the first since the Russian President visited India in Dec 2025 for the annual summit, will follow external affairs minister S Jaishankar’s visit to Moscow this week for a meeting of the 27th India-Russia Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation during which he also called on Putin.

title: Sensex dives 2,200 points in 5 mins, recovers 2,000 points in next 7
content: On Thursday, within a five-minute window after the start of CAS on BSE—between 3.18pm and 3.23pm—sensex crashed over 2,200 points and then within the next seven minutes—between 3.23pm and 3.30pm—it recovered nearly 2,000 points. It finally closed at 76,934 points, down 539 points from its Wednesday close. On NSE, things were relatively quiet. Between 3.18pm and 3.22pm, Nifty slid over 100 points.

title: In 1984, Nasa sent 3,301 bees to space to see how they built honeycomb
content: Thousands of honeybees travelled into space aboard NASA's Space Shuttle Discovery in 1984.  These bees survived microgravity and adapted to their new environment within days.  The mission aimed to observe bee behavior and compare space-built honeycomb.  The bees successfully built approximately 200 cm of honeycomb during the seven-day mission.  Researchers noted differences in cell diameter and wall thickness compared to Earth-made structures.

title: Govt plans to engage third-party auditor to inspect NHs, e-ways
content: EIL had earlier carried out the task of third-party quality check during the construction of the Golden Quadrilateral, the country’s first flagship highway development programme under the then PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee. In recent years, increased instances of deficiencies in NH projects have become a cause of concern, as these have attracted criticism from the public.

title: Kyoto moves bamboo beyond visitors' reach after 350 stalks are vandalised
content: Kyoto’s famous Arashiyama Bamboo Grove is facing growing damage from tourists carving names and other writing into bamboo stalks. A city inspection found around 350 damaged plants since spring 2025. In response, Kyoto officials plan to cut about 30 sq m of bamboo as a special preservation measure and move the grove further away from the path to prevent visitors from reaching the stalks.

title: Sailor spent years alone on Suwarrow before it became a national park
content: Suwarrow atoll, once the secluded refuge of hermit Tom Neale, has transformed into the Cook Islands' inaugural conservation sanctuary. After Neale spent sixteen years in seclusion on Anchorage Island, the atoll was designated as a national park and bird haven. This vital area now protects critical seabird nesting grounds and marine ecosystems, allowing Neale's legacy to be honored through his preserved hut and a tribute on the island.

title: Anthropic tells employees at its San Francisco office to work from home
content: Anthropic asked its employees to work remotely this week due to a potential security guard walkout.  The security contractor, Allied Universal, had warned the AI company about this possibility.  However, the guards' union stated that no strike authorization vote has occurred.  This action by Anthropic appears to be a precautionary measure against an unconfirmed threat.  The company is preparing for a potential initial public offering soon.

title: Trump changes Lake Ontario’s name to ‘Lake America’ amid tensions with Canada
content: Trump signed an executive order on Thursday changing the lake's name for the US geographic naming service. The decision applies to how the body of water is officially identified by US authorities, but Trump has no power to make Canada adopt the new name. The move follows Trump's earlier decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America” for use by the US government.

title: Nepal floods: No adverse impact of flash floods on Indian side, says NDRF
content: NDRF has deployed 20 teams — 11 in UP and nine in Bihar — for evacuation, relief and rescue operations in case these areas experience floods and waterlogging. These include an NDRF team deployed in Kushinagar district, near Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh. In a media briefing, NDRF IG Narendra Bundela said floods have caused massive destruction in Nepal with hundreds of people, including Indian tourists, reported missing.

title: Cedric Tillman’s rise brought hope, struggles raised doubts and end stunned fans
content: With the roster deadline looming, the Cleveland Browns have parted ways with wide receiver Cedric Tillman. This decision reflects the team's commitment to younger, more promising talents at the position. Despite Tillman's adequate performance, it wasn't enough to keep him on the roster. The Kansas City Chiefs could see potential in him as a budget-friendly option, leaving Tillman to seek new opportunities elsewhere in the league.

title: Vince Young’s rise, NFL fallout, bankruptcy and road to redemption
content: From a turbulent childhood to college football acclaim, Vince Young’s story is a testament to perseverance. While his NFL stint with the Tennessee Titans was full of challenges and financial hardships, Young has reclaimed control of his life. Now, he channels his efforts into being a dedicated father, aiming to cultivate a lasting, positive impact for his three kids.

title: Join sports, playgrounds more important than PlayStation: PM to youth
content: Speaking at the Khelo India dialogue, he said, “More important than screens are sports centres. More important than PlayStation is the playground. And this will happen only when the youth embrace this approach.” Lamenting India’s absence from almost half of Olympic sports, he said that is why he had announced a talent hunt for children in the 5-15 years age bracket.

title: HDFC looks to appeal 99.97% haircut on claims against Zee’s Chandra
content: Assenting creditors (80.8%) contested allegations of being related parties and argued that Rs. 6.5-crore plan offered a better outcome compared to pushing the personal guarantor into bankruptcy, since Chandra’s net worth according to the resolution professional was only Rs. 31.8 crore, of which Rs. 25 crore was his mortgaged house. Chandra has disputed the Rs. 22,000-crore liability, stating it reflected historical claims filed in 2022.

title: OpenAI rolls out ChatGPT ads in India, over 50 brands on board
content: From Sept 4, businesses will also get access to a self-serve ChatGPT ads manager, with daily campaign budgets starting at Rs 725, potentially opening the platform to smaller advertisers alongside large brands. An OpenAI spokesperson told TOI that the company expects early advertiser interest across travel, financial services, retail, and health and beauty.

title: BJP cites ‘jhooth ki goonj’ site to hit out at Rahul Gandhi
content: “Rahul’s every lie will be countered with facts. The ‘jhooth ki goonj’ website is exposing every lie of his. The louder propaganda echoes, the faster truth will emerge,” BJP spokesperson Anil Banluni said. Party neta Sudhanshu Trivedi said Rahul is full of frustration and envy vis-a-vis PM Modi, but every lie of his is being exposed.

title: Hours after blocking, X restores account of organisation hosting Bhagwat in New York
content: The @AheadForum1 handle of American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue (AHEAD Forum) became unavailable Wednesday, three days before Bhagwat’s address at Madison Square Garden’s Infosys Theatre. Seeking restoration, AHEAD Forun had earlier said that the suspension “may have occurred in error” and its communications promoted “universal peace, oneness, harmony” and interfaith dialogue. No public evidence links X’s action to protests around the programme.

title: India’s petroleum products’ exports surge 8% in July
content: Govt data showed India exported 2.4 million tonnes (MT) of diesel in July this year, up from 2.2 MT in the corresponding month last year, while total petroleum product exports rose from 5 MT to 5.5 MT. Diesel is currently commanding nearly 70% premium over crude, making exports lucrative for refiners despite the windfall gains tax govt brought in to ensure adequate domestic stocks.

title: Supreme Court issues directions to expedite dowry trials
content: The bench also directed states/Union territories and high courts to conduct periodic training and sensitisation programmes for judicial officers, police officials, prosecutors, protection officers, counsellors through judicial academies, police training institutions and other appropriate bodies. A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih said there was a need for time-bound completion of trial in dowry cases and directed the high courts to periodically review pending criminal appeals.

title: The big IT shake-up: Hiring in GCCs outpaces traditional tech; who gets the job?
content: Global Capability Centres or GCCs which are essentially specialised offshore units of multinational companies are fast absorbing talent from the traditional IT sector. The trend suggests that India’s GCCs are emerging as an increasingly important engine of technology hiring.

title: WWE's what-if! The dream match that never came: One of Vince's biggest misses
content: Despite being two of the most dominant figures in WWE's history, Batista and Brock Lesnar never shared the ring in a singles match. Their careers overlapped, but Lesnar's departure in 2004 allowed Batista to ascend to the top of the promotion. When both superstars made their returns, chances for a showdown were missed. Now, with their wrestling careers behind them, fans can only wonder what might have been.

title: 'Pak deployed spies to find S-400s': Military official's explosive claim on Op Sindoor
content: Pakistan deployed spies and activated sleeper cells to locate S-400 air defence systems. These efforts included satellite support and electronic warfare capabilities from other nations. The S-400 system demonstrated its long-range strike capability during Operation Sindoor. It successfully intercepted a large Pakistani aircraft over 300 kilometers away. India's air defence network has expanded with additional S-400 system deliveries.

title: American eagle vs Canadian goose: How a Goan photographer's US retreat was edited out
content: The White House shared an image of a bald eagle attacking a Canadian goose. This photograph was intended to symbolise American dominance in trade negotiations. However, the actual wildlife event showed the goose fighting back successfully. The eagle eventually abandoned its pursuit, and the image backfired diplomatically. This incident highlights the administration's social media efforts often failing.

title: Nearly one million Indians stuck in US green card backlog; EB-2 wait could stretch to 179 years
content: In the United States, close to one million Indians are bogged down by long-lasting green card backlogs, representing a staggering seventy-nine percent of applicants in these categories. Some Indian professionals may face wait times soaring to an unbelievable 179 years. This issue arises from annual visa caps and per-country limits, highlighting the urgent need for reforms to alleviate the distressing delays faced by skilled workers.

title: Rs 1.1 lakh cr to Rs 2.1 lakh cr: Why cost of 1st bullet train project has doubled
content: The bullet train project is also becoming a platform for India's own high-speed rail ambitions. BEML and ICF are developing India's first indigenous high-speed trainset, with the first expected to roll out in 2027. The trains are being designed for operating speeds of around 250 kmph, with a design speed of 280 kmph.

title: From washing utensils in Kolkata to a career-best 167: Shahbaz's cricket journey
content: Shahbaz Ahmed left civil engineering studies in Haryana to chase cricket dreams in Kolkata, 1,500km from home. Facing financial hardship, he washed dishes and lived in modest club quarters while training. His breakthrough came with Tapan Memorial, followed by Bengal, IPL and India selection. After slipping from contention, Shahbaz returned strongly with 167 runs and 3/20 for East Zone.

title: Happy Raksha Bandhan 2026: Images, wishes, messages, quotes, pictures and greeting cards
content: Raksha Bandhan honors the profound bond that exists between siblings, where brothers and sisters exchange heartfelt wishes and messages to celebrate their connection. This festival promotes virtual connections, allowing loved ones to express their affection despite physical distance. The sacred rakhi thread symbolizes an unwavering promise of love and safety, enriching sibling ties through treasured memories and joyful experiences.

title: How Zohran Mamdani mastered Trump's 'Art of the Deal'
content: Interestingly, Donald Trump laid down 11 rules for successful deal-making inThe Art of the Deal. Mamdani’s first eight months as mayor suggest that he has followed Trump’s rules more faithfully than most people who actually work for Trump.

content: According to the police, the woman worked at a real estate company, while her husband, Yuvraj, is an employee of an aviation company.

content: The orders were issued against Gururaj Joshi, an assistant teacher at Government Girls' High School in Hunasagi, and Anna Saheb Deshmukh, head teacher of Government Lower Primary School at Kuppi in Surpur taluk.
